activity_context.topic_title: Approximating Values Using the Binomial Theorem

examples.knowledge_point: Approximating Powers of Numbers Using the Binomial Theorem
examples.problem: Use the first $3$ terms of the binomial expansion of ${\left( 2+x \right)^{4}}$ in ascending powers of $x$ to approximate $(1.97)^{4}.$

feedback.worked_solution:
Recall that when $n$ is a positive integer, 

$$
(1+x)^{n}=1+nx+\frac{1}{2!}n(n-1){x}^{2}+⋯+{x}^{n}.
$$

Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}{(1+x)}^{5} & =1+5x+\frac{1}{2}\cdot 5\cdot 4\cdot {x}^{2}+⋯+{x}^{5} \\  & =1+5x+10{x}^{2}+⋯+{x}^{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, for small $x,$ we have

$$
{(1+x)}^{5}≈1+5x+10{x}^{2}.
$$

Finally, we substitute $x=-0.11$ into the above approximation of $(1+x)^{5}:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}(0.89)^{5} & =(1+(-0.11))^{5} \\  & ≈1+5(-0.11)+10(-0.11)^{2} \\  & =1-5(0.11)+10(0.012\,1) \\  & =1-0.55+0.121 \\  & ≈0.571,\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to three decimal places.
